Mstow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mstów, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Mstów began developing in the 19th century, reaching 410 people (27 percent) by 1860 and 740 (37.6 percent) by 1921; most of the town's Jews were killed at Treblinka at the end of 1942. This cemetery's land was purchased in 1885 by Moszek Szymonowicz Grylak, sold to the Jewish community the following year, and formally approved for cemetery use in 1887 by Warsaw's chief governor. During WWII, the Germans carried out executions here, including the shooting of seven Jews in summer 1943, and used some matzevot to harden roads by the German mayor's order; in 1947, following intervention by the Jewish Congregation in Częstochowa, 95 whole and about 30 damaged tombstones were recovered from a nearby street pavement and returned. The site later fell into further disrepair, used as pasture and a playground, with more tombstones thrown into the Warta River; in 2015, as part of a research project on the region, about 100 decayed matzevot were recovered from the riverbed and secured by the Mstów Commune Office.
